story.intro: The story walks participants through their own data, a slide at a time, before they decide what to share. Each slide shows one thing about their data, in a sentence and a chart, and can ask about it. Everything is worked out on the participant's device: you never see their data, only their answers, and only when they share them. Slides about data a participant did not add are skipped. Participants see the story once you publish the project.

seen-data.title: Seen data
seen-data.body: **Seen data** is the structure of the data packages seen so far: the names of folders, files and fields, never their contents. Every test package you load adds to it, and so do the structures participants share.

extractor.title: The extractor
extractor.body:
The **extractor** says what to take from the seen data. Each of its **nodes** matches one or more paths in the seen data, and has a **name** and a **decision**: show it to participants, ask them to donate it, or ignore it.

Paths no node matches are **not matched**: nobody has looked at them yet, and they are left out. Click a part that is not matched to match it: give it a name and a decision. Matching a field also matches the folders, files and objects it is in, named by their keys.

names.title: Names
names.body:
**Names** tell participants and researchers how to read the data. Every matched part has one: its key, until you give it a clearer name ("Video title" for titleText). The name decides how data is presented: participants see it, and donations are exported under it, so the data is organised for your analysis.

Tables and columns are named after their nodes: the entries of a list become the rows of a table named after the list. Nodes with the same name form one table or one column.

Names can have a label per language and a description (under More), such as "the time you watched each video", which participants read when they are asked to donate it.

decisions.title: Decisions
decisions.body:
**Show**: participants see it in their own view of their data. Nothing is sent.

**Donate**: participants see it, and are asked to donate it. Only what they agree to is sent, encrypted for your project.

**Ignore**: left out, with everything inside it. Ignored is not the same as not matched: it says someone looked and did not want it.

On a folder, file or object, the decision menu sets the fields inside at once.

same-name.title: Merge, or the same name
same-name.body:
When you give a part a name another part has, Combray asks what you mean.

**Merge into that node**: they are the same data under different keys, such as a field and its translation. They become one node with both keys and one set of settings. This is refused when both keys are in one package side by side: then they hold different data.

**A new node with the same name**: each keeps its own node and settings (its own decision, how it is read), and participants see them as one table or column.

matches.title: Matches and regular expressions
matches.body:
A node matches keys in the files: exact keys, or regular expressions for keys that change, such as a date in a file name. A node with several matches takes the data of each, with the same settings.

If a regular expression matches several keys in one package, the node is split: one node per key, each with a copy of the settings. Find these under Advanced, in the dialog of a matched part.

required.title: Required
required.body: An upload only fits this platform when it has this part, by any of its matches. Use it for parts every package has; a participant without them cannot add their data.

skip-new.title: Skip new parts
skip-new.body: Parts that are new below this node (not in the seen data) are skipped: never opened, shown or offered for structure sharing. That keeps uploads small and the questions short, but you will not hear about renamed or new parts here. The setting passes down to everything inside.

keys-are-data.title: Keys that are data
keys-are-data.body: Sometimes the keys of an object are data rather than names of fields, such as the people who replied or the days of a diary. Then each key becomes a row, with the key and its value as columns. The decision on "each key" is about the keys themselves, such as the names of the people who replied.

read-as.title: Read as
read-as.body:
How a value is read: as a date, a number, a link's domain, and so on. Participants see, and donate, the value as read here.

With a conversion, you can also ask to donate the value as it is in the file, next to the converted one.

clean.title: Cleaning steps
clean.body: Steps applied to a value in order, before it is read, such as trimming spaces or taking a part of a text.

filter-rows.title: Filter rows
filter-rows.body: Conditions the rows of a table must meet, all of them, to be imported. Use them to leave out rows that are not the participant's own activity, such as ads. The button on the row says how many filters it has.

header-row.title: First row holds the column names
header-row.body: For a table whose header is written as an ordinary row, so its columns only have names like #cell[0]. Participants then see the first row's text as the column names, and not as a row. Only how the table is shown changes: the data, and what participants donate, keep the row as it is. Columns you gave a name keep your name.

test-packages.title: Test packages
test-packages.body:
A data download package of your own (the zip or folder you got from the platform) or a synthetic example. Its structure is kept with this platform, so the extractor knows it and everyone in the project sees it. Its values stay in this browser tab, unless you keep them too.

A package loaded for this tab only ("Look at a package") shows its values here and is gone on reload; its structure is kept like any other.

keep-values.title: Keeping the values
keep-values.body: Tick this only for a package that is synthetic or holds nothing sensitive, such as one from a test account you made. Its values are then stored on the server with this project, readable by everyone in the project after signing in, so you can see them without uploading the package again, and preview the story with it. You confirm that this is fine by ticking the box.

undecided-shown.title: Show what is not decided
undecided-shown.body: Off: participants see only what you set to show or donate. On: they also see what is still not matched or undecided, including parts that are new since you last looked. Either way, participants can switch to "Raw data" to see their whole package as it is.

find.title: Finding the package
find.body: Participants pick their package as a zip, a folder or a file, and that is tried first, without looking at its name. If it does not fit, Combray looks inside it for files or folders with one of these names, such as Takeout or watch-history*.json. Use * as a wildcard; letters can be upper or lower case.

conflict.title: Two keys side by side
conflict.body: This node matches two different keys that are next to each other in one package, so it is not clear which value is meant. Make its matches narrower, or split it into one node per key (under Advanced).

name-mismatch.title: Different decisions under one name
name-mismatch.body: Nodes with this name have different decisions. Each keeps its own decision for its own data, which is allowed but unusual: participants see one column with a mix.
